title: What If Earth Sat at the Center of the Milky Way?

scenes.text: What if Earth sat at the center of the Milky Way? The night sky would never go dark.
Right now we're about eight thousand parsecs out, in a quiet suburb with roughly one star in every five cubic parsecs.
Near the center, there are about ten million stars in every cubic parsec. That's fifty million times denser.
The sky would be ablaze with stars, a dazzling display day and night, and the stars would be the least of it.
At the very middle sits a black hole about two and a half million times the mass of our Sun.
Astronomers would hate it, and so would any planet there. The quiet suburb we live in is the lucky spot.
